question.text: The Incan empire was centered in this modern day country, whose capital is Lima.
question.clue: The Paracas culture was centered on this country, where the Chimu preceded the Moche culture, and produced textiles that were woven using alpaca wool.

swap.text: This Spaniard led the war against the Incas and ordered the execution of Atahualpa, even though Atahualpa offered to give this man a room filled with gold.
swap.clue: This man received help from longtime partner Diego Almagro, but he was killed by Almagro's forces in the Battle of Las Salinas.

question.text: This Incan "lost city" is believed to have been built for Pachacuti. It was re-discovered in 1911 by Hiram Bingham.
question.clue: Hiram Bingham ("HEE-rum BING-hum") publicized the existence of this site.

swap.leadin: Tupac Amaru's 1572 uprising could not reverse the fate of this empire.
swap.text: Identify this empire that was weakened by the civil war between the sons of Huayna Capac.
swap.clue: One ruler of these people allegedly gained a fortune from places termed the "Outer Belt" and the "Fire Belt," and another earned a name meaning "overturner of the world" or "earthshaker" after stones supposedly came to life to help him repel Chanka invaders.

question.leadin: Name some things about the downfall of the Incan Empire.
question.text: The downfall of the Incan empire began when Pizarro launched this surprise attack on the royal Incan family. Pizarro's capture of the Inca here led to him demanding a room full of gold as ransom.
question.clue: The losing side in this battle was engaged in a civil war against Huascar and was crippled by the decision to leave the bulk of its army outside the city walls.

swap.leadin: In its native Quechua tongue it is known as Tawantinsuyu or "Land of the Four Quarters"
swap.text: Identify this empire conquered by the Spanish and whose mita system was used by the Spanish to run the silver mines at Potosi.
swap.clue: Runners trekked 200 miles a day in this empire to share messages.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Andean civilizations.
question.text: This culture existed in the Ica river valley succeeding the Paracas culture. These people are famous for theirnamesake lines which form geoglyphs visible from the sky.

swap.leadin: Name the following regarding the Wiphala [wi-PAH-lah].
swap.text: Andeans speak this indigenous language, which also names them. It is a primary language group, also called Runa Simi.
swap.clue: The MUPP-NP party's common name is a word in this language that's gained popularity with indigenists for its connotation of "world reversal."

question.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
question.text: One of the leaders of this confederation ritually covered himself in gold dust before diving into Lake Guatavita. This confederation, which was led by a Zipa and a Zaque ["ZAH-kay"], held territory in the highlands of modern-day Colombia.
question.clue: Perhaps this polity's most well-known artefact is known as this polity's "raft", which is a gold sculpture that was found in Lake Guatavita.

swap.leadin: A first-year undergrad named Manny Medrano helped decode a system used in these things.
swap.text: Identify these records made from alpaca and llama fibers, most commonly used for keeping track of tribute.
swap.clue: The coarsest wool was instead woven by commoners and used to make chusi, a cloth used for ch'uspa sacks and blankets, or the knotted cords that comprise these recordkeeping devices.

question.text: This Inca city was shaped like a puma and served as the capital of the empire. Legend holds that it was built by Pachacuti.
question.clue: Juan Veramendi erected a Basilica Cathedral here, and Vicente Valverde served as the first bishop of this city, where Diego Almagro was executed.

swap.leadin: Answer some stuff about the geography of Ecuador.
swap.text: This high active volcano sits just south of Quito and destroyed the city of Tacunga in 1698 with an eruption.

question.leadin: Construction with this quality, visible at the Acllahuasi at Cuzco, necessitated masons to precisely shape stones to fit with other pieces on site.
question.text: Name or describe this limitation of the rubble masonry in Incan walls. The term "drystone" refers to masonry made with this limitation.
question.answerHtml: built without mortar [accept answer involving no fill or material between stones]

swap.text: This emperor of the Inca wrote special hymns for the Situa Festival. This man, whose name means "Earthshaker," pacified the Chanca peoples and his son, Tupo Inca, built the Saqsaywaman Fort in Cusco.
swap.clue: This ruler, who legendarily subjugated the (+) Chanka people with stone warriors, organized his realm into four suyus.

question.text: This Incan ruler lost a civil war to his half-brother Atahualpa, after their father Huayna Capac's death from smallpox led to a succession crisis.
question.clue: After the death of his father Huayna Capac, Atahualpa fought this brother for control of the Inca Empire. He was defeated and imprisoned after losses at Chimborazo and Quipaipan.

swap.leadin: After being attacked by the rival Chanka people, this ruler is said to have called on the sun god Inti to turn stones into pururauca warriors to defend his city.
swap.text: Name this son of Viracocha who transformed the Kingdom of Cuzco into the Incan Empire in the 15th century.
swap.clue: This king commissioned life-sized gold statues of animals and plant for the central garden of his Coricancha temple.

question.text: Under the "fictive reciprocity" of mit'a, laborers were supplied with large feasts and gifts of this substance. The sequestered aclla("AHK-yah"), or "chosen women," chewed maize to prepare this good for elite ceremonies.
question.clue: Chasquis runners carried this traditional fermented alcoholic beverage of the Inca. Women called aqlla lived in compounds their entire lives performing ceremonial tasks such as brewing this beverage.

swap.leadin: Identify some more things about the history of New Spain.
swap.text: This fifth Viceroy of Peru instituted namesake civil reforms after being appointed in 1568. His accomplishments include a less exploitative labor system and the execution of Tupac Amaru.

question.leadin: Identify these much-regarded military commanders from South American history, FTPE.
question.text: This huge badass burned Quito to the ground and killed its virgins to deny them to Pizarro's forces after losing the Battle of Mount Chimborazo to Belalcazar. Supposedly, he took the location of the Llanganatis Treasure to his grave, and with Quizquiz and Chalicuchima, commanded the Incan forces of Atahualpa.

swap.leadin: They were put forth by the namesake Count of Oropesa and overturned the New Laws of Blasco Nunez Vela.
swap.text: Name this set of structural changes put forth in the 1570s, which created "reductions" of native population governed by kuraka, and established the mita system for forced labor in the silver mines.
swap.clue: Spain revived the mita system in this series of late 16th-century laws, which installed Inca regional leaders called kurakas as the head of repartimientos, or groups of natives from whom labor could be levied.
